title: Regrow functional nephrons inside an adult human kidney

concept.text: The proposed innovation is controlled adult nephrogenesis: forming new, functional filtering units inside an adult human kidney that has lost nephrons. Adult kidneys do not normally replace these units. Achieving this capability would mean rebuilding part of the existing organ’s filtering machinery after loss.

As a functional requirement of the proposed innovation, each new nephron would need an effective blood supply, a working filtration barrier and tubule, and a connection to urinary drainage. The new units would also need to coordinate with surrounding tissue. Producing kidney-like structures or increasing a molecular marker would not by itself establish that these requirements had been met.

The defining advance would be initiating nephron formation in adulthood within an injured kidney. Increasing nephron numbers during development, restoring the performance of surviving nephrons, and enlarging existing units are biologically distinct outcomes. All could improve kidney function, but only convincing evidence of newly formed units would establish the proposed adult regenerative capability.

significance.text: If new nephrons could be generated safely and integrated durably, lost filtering capacity could become a repairable deficit within the patient’s existing kidney. This would change a central limitation of adult kidney biology: nephron loss is normally not offset by production of replacement units. The supplied developmental study provides a biological foothold for manipulating nephron formation, while leaving adult repair unproven.

Conditional downstream possibilities include preserving useful kidney function longer and allowing some patients to avoid or delay dialysis or transplantation. Those benefits would depend on how much capacity could be restored, how long it lasted, and whether the underlying disease remained active. The ability to make new nephrons would not by itself establish that dialysis could be eliminated broadly or that every cause and stage of kidney disease could be treated.

A key limit on the regeneration analogy is that increasing nephron endowment while a kidney is developing does not establish that the same intervention can restart construction in a mature, injured organ. Likewise, improved whole-kidney filtration after developmental treatment does not establish the independent functional contribution of each additional unit. The revolutionary consequence therefore remains conditional on adult formation, integration, sustained function and safety.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved capability in the supplied evidence is restarting and controlling nephron formation after the normal developmental window has closed. The reviewed study manipulated developmental nephrogenesis; it did not demonstrate initiation of new nephron formation in an injured adult human kidney. A route from developmental pathway control to adult regeneration remains to be established.

Engineering requirements inferred from the intended function include establishing a suitable source of nephron-forming cells, directing their organization into complete filtering units, connecting them to circulation and urinary outflow, and supporting their maturation within damaged tissue. These requirements must be met together: anatomical formation without useful drainage or perfusion would not restore the intended kidney function. The supplied study does not resolve these adult integration problems.

Growth control is a substantive barrier. In the neonatal experiments, the effect of activating the SAM–METTL3 pathway depended on dose. A higher M3A dose produced smaller kidneys and reduced glomerular counts, whereas higher SAM dosing lost the benefit seen at lower dosing. These observations support the need for a controlled treatment window; they do not establish that high-dose SAM itself was toxic. Whether a safe and effective adult treatment window exists remains unknown.

For the proposed adult therapy, regeneration would also need to proceed without uncontrolled growth, deterioration of surviving tissue or worsening of the underlying disease. A further challenge is measurement: investigators must separate formation of additional nephrons from recovery or enlargement of existing units and then determine how much the new units contribute to sustained function. These are proposed translational requirements, rather than achievements of the developmental study.

current_state.text: Ramalingam and colleagues reported developmental manipulation of nephron formation in “An RNA transmethylation pathway governs kidney nephrogenic potential,” published in Nature Communications on May 28, 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-60097-6. The supplied review examined the full main article and found support for increased neonatal glomerular counts at selected treatment doses and higher filtration estimates later in life. This is published developmental evidence, not a demonstration of adult human nephron regeneration.

The newborn mouse experiments targeted a period when nephrogenesis was still occurring: the article describes mouse nephron formation as persisting for approximately four days after birth. Selected doses of SAM–METTL3 pathway activation increased glomerular counts during this developmental setting. Follow-up after the animals matured does not change the timing of the intervention into adult-onset regeneration.

The article reports a statistically significant 20% increase in estimated glomerular filtration rate after neonatal SAM treatment, assessed later using FITC-sinistrin. This is a whole-kidney functional association; it does not isolate the filtration contribution of individual additional nephrons. The article inconsistently identifies the later filtration measurement as postnatal day 35 or day 40, so the precise timing remains unresolved in the supplied review.

The developmental response was not uniformly beneficial across doses. Higher M3A exposure was associated with smaller kidneys and fewer glomeruli, while higher SAM exposure did not retain the lower-dose benefit. The useful conclusion is that pathway activation had a dose-dependent effect on developmental nephron formation. The findings do not justify treating all stronger activation as beneficial or assigning the same adverse effect to both interventions.

Interpretive limits remain. Glomerular counts used acid maceration, and investigators were not blinded. Although the full main text was available to the reviewer, figures and supplementary data were not supplied for independent visual or numerical inspection. The reported qualitative findings and 20% filtration estimate therefore rest on the main-text assessment described in the supplied review. These limitations constrain independent verification; they do not establish that the reported results are false.

The supplied evidence contains no adult human regenerative experiment. It also contains no freshness search establishing subsequent developments or confirming the field’s status through November 1, 2026. The supported account is therefore the reviewed 2025 developmental result and its limits; the materials do not establish an exhaustive, up-to-date survey of adult kidney regeneration.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: in adults with substantial nephron loss, show newly formed nephrons inside the existing kidney, with anatomically verified blood supply and urinary drainage. Use lineage tracing where feasible, or comparably persuasive evidence suitable for the setting, to distinguish formation of new units from enlargement or recovery of surviving ones. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not an established consensus standard.
completion_criteria.label: New nephrons have verified blood supply and urinary drainage

completion_criteria.text: Proposed functional demonstration: establish that the newly formed units make a measurable contribution to sustained filtration and that treatment improves clinically meaningful outcomes. Whole-kidney improvement should be accompanied by evidence connecting that improvement to the additional units, with appropriate comparisons addressing recovery of existing tissue and other competing explanations. Anatomical findings and functional benefit should reinforce one another.
completion_criteria.label: New nephrons sustain measurable filtration and improve clinically meaningful outcomes

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and safety requirements: reproduce the result independently, use blinded assessment where feasible, and follow recipients long enough to evaluate durability, uncontrolled growth, injury to surviving tissue and worsening disease. An actual protocol would need to specify meaningful effect sizes, acceptable risks and follow-up duration; the supplied materials do not establish numerical thresholds for these decisions.
completion_criteria.label: Regeneration is independently reproduced with durability and safety follow-up

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundaries: report which disease settings, degrees of nephron loss and tissue conditions permit useful regeneration, together with treatment and monitoring requirements. Success in a defined patient group could establish a meaningful capability without establishing effectiveness in every kidney disease. Finite studies demonstrate the breadth tested; claims of broad dialysis avoidance or universal applicability would require additional evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Report regeneration boundaries and required treatment and monitoring

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison with NEP-02, “Rebuild function in scarred kidneys by reversing established fibrosis”: fibrosis reversal addresses the damaged tissue environment, while NEP-01 requires formation of additional filtering units. The approaches could be complementary if scar reduction enabled regeneration, but recovered function after fibrosis reversal would not by itself demonstrate new nephrons.

Roster-based comparison with NEP-03, “Manufacture transplantable human kidneys from cells”: both concepts require organized kidney tissue, vascular integration and useful function. NEP-03 aims to manufacture a replacement organ for transplantation; NEP-01 aims to add functional units within an adult’s existing kidney. Success in either setting would leave important integration requirements specific to the other.

Roster-based comparison with NEP-04, “A durable, implantable artificial kidney,” and NEP-05, “Kidney replacement that is portable and affordable at global scale”: these concepts address replacement of kidney function through devices or scalable treatment delivery. NEP-01 pursues biological restoration within the native organ. Their clinical goals overlap, while durability, access, affordability and delivery remain separate questions from whether adult nephrogenesis can be achieved.

Roster-based comparison with NEP-06, “An effectively unlimited supply of durable animal-donor kidneys,” and NEP-07, “Reliably induce donor-specific tolerance in kidney recipients”: these concepts address replacement-organ supply and immune acceptance, respectively. NEP-01 seeks restoration within the existing organ and could reduce replacement demand if effective. Its own immune requirements would depend on the eventual cell source and treatment method, which remain unspecified.

Roster-based comparison with NEP-08, “A root-cause, durable treatment for ADPKD,” and NEP-09, “Durable reversal of diabetic kidney disease”: these concepts target particular disease processes. NEP-01 targets replacement of lost nephron capacity and does not inherently remove the cause of continuing damage. Disease control and regeneration could be complementary; new units would still need protection from the condition that injured the original tissue.

Roster-based comparison with NEP-10, “Broad prevention of severe acute kidney injury”: preventing injury could preserve existing nephrons and reduce the need for regeneration. NEP-01 addresses formation of replacement units after loss. Recovery following acute injury must still be distinguished from production of new nephrons before it can count as evidence for this concept.

unresolved_issues: Whether developmental SAM–METTL3 pathway manipulation can enable safe nephron formation in an injured adult kidney remains unestablished by the supplied evidence.
The adult cell source, delivery method, vascular and urinary integration strategy, and effective growth-control window remain unspecified.
The article’s postnatal day 35 versus day 40 filtration-assessment discrepancy remains unresolved.
Figures and supplementary data were unavailable for independent inspection in the supplied review.
The evidence does not isolate how much of the later whole-kidney filtration increase came from additional nephrons.
No supplied freshness search establishes subsequent developments or comprehensive field status through November 1, 2026.
Clinical effect-size thresholds, safety boundaries, follow-up duration and eligible disease settings require definition in an actual demonstration protocol.

brief.title: New filtering units inside an adult kidney
possible: People who have lost kidney function could regrow nephrons, the kidney’s filtering units, inside their own damaged organ. The new units would filter blood and send waste into urine, rebuilding some of the capacity they had lost.
why: Adult kidneys do not normally replace lost nephrons. Making replacements could help people keep useful kidney function longer and delay or avoid dialysis, a treatment that cleans the blood, or a kidney transplant.

sources.showed: Treating newborn mice while their kidneys were still developing increased filtering-unit counts at selected doses. Estimated kidney filtration was 20% higher later in life after one treatment.
sources.quote: targeting this pathway enhances murine nephron endowment.
sources.cited_for: Kidney development can be altered to produce more filtering units in mice.
sources.not_established: The treatment did not restart nephron formation in an injured adult kidney or isolate how much the extra units contributed to filtration.

sources.showed: They identified clusters of precursor cells, which can develop into nephrons, in adult zebrafish. Transplanted clusters generated new nephrons in adult recipients.
sources.quote: Here we trace the source of new nephrons in the adult zebrafish to small cellular aggregates containing nephron progenitors.
sources.cited_for: Adult nephron formation is possible in zebrafish, and cells responsible for it can be transplanted.
sources.not_established: The work does not establish an equivalent cell source or regenerative treatment in adult humans.

sources.showed: Mouse and rat precursor cells formed nephrons connected to urine drainage in newborn mice, with lasting survival and signs of function. Human precursor cells also formed nephrons there.
sources.quote: Additionally, induced human nephron progenitor cells differentiate into nephrons within the neonatal kidneys.
sources.cited_for: Developing mouse kidneys can support added nephrons and their connection to urine drainage.
sources.not_established: The work did not demonstrate durable, functioning human nephrons inside an injured adult human kidney.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated different parts of the goal in animals. Diep and colleagues generated nephrons in adult zebrafish. Matsui and colleagues connected added nephrons to urine drainage in developing mouse kidneys.
Ramalingam and colleagues increased nephron counts during mouse development and measured better filtration later. These results have not established regrowth inside an injured adult human kidney.
missing: A treatment must restart nephron formation after normal kidney development has ended and distinguish new units from repaired or enlarged survivors.
New units must develop a blood supply, working filters and tubes, and urine drainage within damaged adult tissue.
The added units must provide lasting filtration without uncontrolled growth, damage to surviving tissue or worsening disease.

milestones.label: New nephrons have blood supply and urine drainage
milestones.explanation: Adults with substantial nephron loss would have to develop demonstrably new units inside their kidneys, with blood supply and urine drainage. This would establish connected replacements rather than recovery of surviving units.

milestones.label: New nephrons sustain filtration and improve health outcomes
milestones.explanation: The added units would have to contribute measurably to lasting filtration, and treatment would have to improve meaningful health outcomes. This would connect new anatomy to useful kidney repair.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce lasting, safe regeneration
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce the result, with blinded assessment where feasible and follow-up for lasting function, abnormal growth and injury. This would test whether regeneration is reliable and safe over time.

milestones.label: Effective treatment settings and monitoring needs are defined
milestones.explanation: Studies would have to establish which diseases, degrees of nephron loss and tissue conditions allow useful regeneration, alongside treatment and monitoring needs. This would define who could benefit and what care they would need.

uncertain: It remains unclear whether the mechanism that increased nephron formation during development can safely restart it in an injured adult kidney.
The source of adult nephron-forming cells, how to deliver them and how to control their growth remain unresolved.
Meaningful benefit, acceptable risk and the length of follow-up needed to judge success still need definition.

page.title: In situ nephron regeneration in adult human kidneys
page.definition: After nephron loss, treatment begun in adulthood causes whole new nephrons to form inside the patient’s kidney. In each new unit, a cluster of small blood vessels called a glomerulus filters the patient’s blood. The attached tubule returns needed substances to the blood, removes additional wastes and delivers the remaining fluid to the kidney’s existing urinary drainage.

goal.need: In 2023, about 831,000 people in the United States were receiving dialysis or living with a kidney transplant. In-center hemodialysis usually takes about four hours three times a week. Adult kidneys do not normally replace lost filtering units. For someone approaching kidney failure, adding nephrons in their own kidney could delay the need for dialysis if the new units restore enough function and keep working.

completion.title: New nephrons filter blood and drain into the urinary system inside an adult human kidney.
completion.criterion: An intervention begun in adulthood generates new glomerulus–tubule units within a human kidney that has lost nephrons. Evidence distinguishes their formation from repair or enlargement of surviving units. In the new units, demonstrate host blood perfusion, passage of filtrate from glomerulus into tubule, tubular transport and continuity with the host urinary drainage.
completion.set_by: Atlas; no externally published completion test specific to adult human nephron regeneration was located.
completion.basis: The NIDDK programme treats increased nephron number and improved function of existing nephrons as distinct outcomes. Adult zebrafish transplantation experiments linked donor origin, uptake of a filtered tracer and connection to host tubules. The adult-human test requires evidence at the level of the new unit. No external minimum nephron count, functional gain or follow-up duration was identified.

milestones.title: An intervention increases nephron number within a living kidney.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate that an intervention increases the number of nephrons inside a living kidney. Establish the increase in nephron number independently of any change in the filtration capacity of surviving units. The programme specifies no minimum increase.
milestones.set_by: NIDDK, RFA-DK-14-010, Section I, UH3 research objectives; the nephron-number branch of its published target.
milestones.threshold_quote: increase nephron number or nephron efficiency in situ to increase kidney capacity

milestones.title: Host vessels perfuse implanted kidney tissue sufficiently to sustain its cells and physiological functions.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate blood flow from host vessels through implanted kidney tissue at a level sufficient to maintain cell health and physiological functions in that tissue. The roadmap specifies no minimum flow or duration.
milestones.set_by: Kidney Health Initiative, KRT Roadmap, Biological and Immunological Modulation; the published target concerns implanted cellular products.
milestones.threshold_quote: Recruit host vessels to implanted cellular product and demonstrate perfusion of implanted tissue that is sufficient to maintain cell health and physiological functions

milestones.title: New nephrons filter blood and connect to urinary drainage in an injured adult mammalian kidney.
milestones.criterion: Begin the intervention in an injured adult mammal after normal nephron formation has ended. Establish that new glomerulus–tubule units form inside the injured kidney and distinguish them from surviving units. Demonstrate host perfusion, filtration into the new tubules, tubular transport and continuity with host urinary drainage.
milestones.set_by: Atlas; searches of RBK calls, KHI roadmaps and nephrogenesis trials found no adult-mammal integration criterion. NIDDK RFA-DK-19-007 supplies the broader goal of restoring function in injury or disease models.

milestones.title: An adult receives a treatment intended to generate nephrons in the native kidney in an authorised study.
milestones.criterion: An adult with nephron loss actually receives an intervention intended to generate new nephrons inside the native kidney in a clinical study. For the US investigational-drug route, the investigational new drug application (IND) must be effective and the protocol approved by an institutional review board. The IND normally takes effect 30 days after FDA receipt unless placed on clinical hold, or earlier on FDA notification. Starting treatment satisfies this milestone; it does not establish nephrogenesis.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Phase 1 IND Frequently Asked Questions, questions 8–9; this specifies the US clinical route.
milestones.threshold_quote: An investigator may not administer an investigational new drug to human subjects until the IND goes into effect

milestones.title: A newly formed nephron connects to the host kidney’s urinary collecting system.
milestones.criterion: Identify a newly formed nephron and demonstrate a continuous lumen from its tubule into the host kidney’s urinary drainage. A connection may run through a host tubule. The evidence must identify the junction with the host, since a collecting duct confined to a graft establishes only drainage within the graft.
milestones.set_by: Renal developmental biology convention described at the September 2018 NIDDK Advisory Council meeting and applied in zebrafish and neonatal mouse studies.
milestones.threshold_quote: the interconnection of the nephrons to the host collecting system

not_found: No registered adult-human study was found whose endpoint verifies newly formed nephrons with filtration and host urinary drainage.
No external numerical requirement was found for adult-onset mammalian nephrogenesis, its functional contribution or its durability.
The full text of the 6 November 2026 kidney-replacement roadmap could not be accessed; its PubMed abstract was accessible.
No NIDDK or Kidney Health Initiative position was found judging induced adult-human nephron formation infeasible or unworthy of pursuit.
No programme, regulator or society criterion was found for verifying both the origin and integrated function of a new nephron in an adult human kidney.

results.detail: The contralateral kidney remained functional, limiting what postoperative blood and urine measurements could establish about the reimplanted kidney. The 48 h optical quantification used one kidney, while 48 h histology used biopsies from three independent experiments.
results.quote: organoid-derived cells remained viable for at least 48 h after in vivo transplantation

results.finding: Human organoid grafts in NOD-SCID mice (n=3 per harvest group) showed modest tubular growth over 2 weeks.
results.detail: The organoids already contained nephron-like structures before implantation. Growth of those structures does not establish an increase in the number of nephrons.

results.finding: Human kidney organoid grafts in mice (n=3 per harvest group) contained host endothelial cells by day 14.
results.detail: Histology showed vascular ingrowth and partial structural maturation. The study did not demonstrate filtration or tubular transport.
results.quote: Kidney organoid grafts survived for months after transplantation and became vascularized from host mouse endothelial cells.

results.finding: Human kidney organoid grafts in mice with ureteral obstruction (n unspecified) survived and vascularized at 2 weeks.
results.detail: The Results text and Methods place follow-up at 14 days. The Figure 7a caption labels the staining as 7 days after obstruction.

results.finding: Host-perfused mouse kidney assembloids had 57.3-fold higher cyst-fluid creatinine than serum (n=3 graft samples).
results.detail: The sample size applies to cyst-fluid chemistry. Intravital imaging separately demonstrated host blood flow through the graft glomeruli and tracer passage into Bowman’s space.
results.quote: Both creatinine and urea were enriched 57.3-fold and 20.2-fold respectively in the cyst fluid (11.47 ± 1.99 mg/dL, and 433.14 ± 10.75 mg/dL) when compared to serum (0.20 ± 0.06 mg/dL, and 21.43 ± 2.33 mg/dL, respectively;

results.finding: Human kidney grafts showed nephron-to-graft collecting duct connections at about 1 month (wild-type cohort n=17 mice, imaging n unstated).
results.detail: The cohort size covers wild-type transplantation overall. The text gives no sample size for the junction imaging or count of connected nephrons.
results.quote:
Elongated renal tubules formed
in vivo
, with their distal ends connected to the central CD

results.finding: Human kidney organoid sheets in NSG mice (six implantations) retained host-perfused glomeruli that filtered 3 kDa dextran.
results.detail: The sample size refers to reported implantation procedures. The paper gives no separate count of grafts with successful filtration.
results.quote: This observation provided evidence of the successful anastomosis of human organoid vessels with the host’s circulatory system, facilitating the filtration of LMW dextran performed by implanted nephron sheets.

results.finding: Human nephron sheets in NSG mice (six implantations) showed passage of 3 kDa dextran into Bowman’s space and uptake by proximal tubular cells.
results.detail: Tracer localization supports tubular uptake and suggests reabsorption. The direct transepithelial cation transport assay used cultured organoids. The grafts lacked collecting ducts.
results.quote: Taken together, both live-cell imaging and fixed tissue analyses suggest that LMW dextran undergoes glomerular filtration and subsequent reabsorption into the interstitial space via tubules.

results.finding: Porcine kidney matrix implants (glomerular counts n=3) contained glomerulus-like and tubular structures at 28 days.
results.detail: The study did not compare whole-kidney nephron counts or verify that each counted glomerulus belonged to a complete glomerulus–tubule unit.
results.quote: Twenty-eight days after implantation, glomeruli, vessels, and renal tubules, characteristic of nephrons, were histologically observed within the matrix.

results.finding: Porcine kidney matrix implants (CT n=3) showed host blood flow at 28 days.
results.detail: Filtration and tubular transport were inferred from structural features and were not measured in the implant.
results.quote: Angiography and dynamic CT allowed imaging active blood flow in a part of the implanted matrix.

results.finding: Porcine kidney matrix implants showed weak urographic enhancement around the matrix at 28 days (urography n unreported).
results.detail: The urographic signal was not localized to a lumen crossing the graft–host boundary.
results.quote: An influx of a contrast agent inside the matrix was also observed using urography.

results.finding: Partially nephrectomized pigs (glomerular counts and CT each n=3) had nephron-like structures and graft perfusion at 28 days.
results.detail: The Methods give a body weight of approximately 20 kg and omit age. Imaging established perfusion of part of the matrix without tracing blood and filtrate through an identified new unit.
results.quote: Our porcine model demonstrated that the implanted organ-derived extracellular matrix induced the structural regeneration of glomeruli, renal tubules, and vessels, and supported the regeneration of their continuous structures as well as the resultant active blood flow.

results.finding: Ten adults with late stage 4 diabetic kidney disease received 19 REACT injections into their native kidneys.
results.detail: The paper reports FDA endorsement of administering both injections into the same kidney. It gives no IND effective date or equivalent confirmation that the IND was effective for this protocol.
results.quote: Five men and 5 women underwent 19 REACT injections (1 participant received only one injection).

results.finding: In adult wild-type zebrafish, 10 of 12 newly formed nephron tubules were positive for fluorescent dextran.
results.detail: Figure 1C locates the host junction directly. The dextran count in Figure 7J measures tracer uptake as supporting evidence of fluid flow. The text gives no sample size for the junction imaging.
results.quote: In wild type, EdU +  new tubules were also positive for dextran ( Fig. 7J ; 10/12 tubules; 83%), indicating fluid flow and successful connections had been established.

results.finding: Of 53 randomized adults with diabetes and chronic kidney disease, 49 received rilparencel by native-kidney injection.
results.detail: The trial assessed safety and change in eGFR slope. Reduced eGFR establishes impaired filtration, while nephron loss was not directly measured. FDA protocol approval is reported without explicit IND status.
results.quote: Fifty-three participants were randomized and 49 received at least one injection.

results.finding: Adult rats with perfused embryonic kidney grafts (n=5) had about 15% of healthy-control creatinine clearance after bilateral nephrectomy.
results.detail: Lectin traced perfusion qualitatively, with no volumetric flow measurement. Urine concentration remained impaired, and survival depended on postoperative support. Creatinine clearance may overestimate filtration.

results.finding: Six2-Cre mice with one Tsc1 allele deleted in nephron progenitors averaged 26,640 nephrons across both kidneys at day 30 (sample size unstated in supplied text).
results.detail: The deletion restored nephron counts to wild-type levels in two mouse models. Two observers independently counted nephrons while blinded to genotype.
results.quote:
by contrast, the average nephron number in Tsc1 -hemi-
zygous kidneys (26,640± 514, P = 0.66) was indistinguishable from
wild-type kidneys and was significantly higher than in Six2TGC+/tg
kidneys (P < 0.0001).

definition = "After nephron loss, treatment begun in adulthood causes whole new nephrons to form inside the patient\u2019s kidney. In each new unit, a cluster of small blood vessels called a glomerulus filters the patient\u2019s blood. The attached tubule returns needed substances to the blood, removes additional wastes and delivers the remaining fluid to the kidney\u2019s existing urinary drainage.". Reason: The definition names the two parts of a nephron and explains what each must do in a newly formed unit.

goal.need = "In 2023, about 831,000 people in the United States were receiving dialysis or living with a kidney transplant. In-center hemodialysis usually takes about four hours three times a week. Adult kidneys do not normally replace lost filtering units. For someone approaching kidney failure, adding nephrons in their own kidney could delay the need for dialysis if the new units restore enough function and keep working.". Reason: The revision dates the treatment burden and explains what sufficient recovery of native kidney function would mean for a patient.

add statement by National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases, (Re)Building a Kidney, RFA-DK-19-007, 2019: "increase nephron number or nephron function". Reason: The 2019 programme call explicitly identifies increased nephron number as one route to restoring function in an injured or diseased kidney.

edit completion: criterion = "An intervention begun in adulthood generates new glomerulus\u2013tubule units within a human kidney that has lost nephrons. Evidence distinguishes their formation from repair or enlargement of surviving units. In the new units, demonstrate host blood perfusion, passage of filtrate from glomerulus into tubule, tubular transport and continuity with the host urinary drainage."; basis = "The NIDDK programme treats increased nephron number and improved function of existing nephrons as distinct outcomes. Adult zebrafish transplantation experiments linked donor origin, uptake of a filtered tracer and connection to host tubules. The adult-human test requires evidence at the level of the new unit. No external minimum nephron count, functional gain or follow-up duration was identified."; refs = [3, 5, 8, 9, 18, 19, 23]. Reason: The criterion makes clear that filtration, transport and drainage must be attributable to the new units, and the basis explains why whole-kidney measurements cannot establish their origin.

edit m1: criterion = "Demonstrate that an intervention increases the number of nephrons inside a living kidney. Establish the increase in nephron number independently of any change in the filtration capacity of surviving units. The programme specifies no minimum increase."; threshold_quote = "increase nephron number or nephron efficiency in situ to increase kidney capacity"; threshold_ref = 3; refs = [3, 8, 24]. Reason: The revised test retains NIDDK’s nephron-number target and removes zebrafish study results from the criterion.

edit m2: title = "Host vessels perfuse implanted kidney tissue sufficiently to sustain its cells and physiological functions."; criterion = "Demonstrate blood flow from host vessels through implanted kidney tissue at a level sufficient to maintain cell health and physiological functions in that tissue. The roadmap specifies no minimum flow or duration."; threshold_quote = "Recruit host vessels to implanted cellular product and demonstrate perfusion of implanted tissue that is sufficient to maintain cell health and physiological functions"; threshold_ref = 6. Reason: The Kidney Health Initiative’s perfusion target applies to implanted cellular tissue, and the mouse survival and engraftment figures do not measure that target.

add milestone after m2: "A newly formed nephron connects to the host kidney’s urinary collecting system.". Reason: Connection to host urinary drainage is a distinct integration step that can be demonstrated before the combined adult-mammal test.

edit m3: criterion = "Begin the intervention in an injured adult mammal after normal nephron formation has ended. Establish that new glomerulus\u2013tubule units form inside the injured kidney and distinguish them from surviving units. Demonstrate host perfusion, filtration into the new tubules, tubular transport and continuity with host urinary drainage."; refs = [2, 5, 8, 9, 18, 23]. Reason: The criterion retains the adult-onset requirement and removes whole-kidney filtration results from mice treated as newborns.

edit m4: title = "An adult receives a treatment intended to generate nephrons in the native kidney in an authorised study.". Reason: The existing title implies demonstrated nephron generation, although the milestone is reached when an adult receives a treatment intended to generate nephrons.
structure = parallel. Reason: Host perfusion and connection to urinary drainage can be tested independently, although the integrated adult-mammal milestone requires both.

add not found: "No NIDDK or Kidney Health Initiative position was found judging induced adult-human nephron formation infeasible or unworthy of pursuit.". Reason: A statement about the limits of natural adult kidney repair would not establish an institutional objection to induced regeneration.

add not found: "No programme, regulator or society criterion was found for verifying both the origin and integrated function of a new nephron in an adult human kidney.". Reason: The existing search notes cover trial endpoints and numerical requirements but omit the question of who defines the combined biological test.
remove statement 1. Reason: The Kidney Health Initiative’s patient roadmap names recovery of kidney function as a goal without specifying that new nephrons must form.
